newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Peres says Netanyahu must resign despite report.
newsitem.headline: Peres says Netanyahu must resign despite report.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres called for Benjamin Netanyahu's resignation on Sunday even though prosecutors decided not to charge the prime minister in a corruption scandal.

"There's not enough evidence to put the prime minister on trial but there is enough evidence to place the prime minister again before the judgment of the people," Peres told Israel Radio, demanding new elections.

Labour leader Peres, defeated by Likud leader Netanyahu in an election last May, said: "It's inconceivable that this prime minister will walk under such a heavy shadow of nonconfidence, of very heavy accusations whose only weakness is that they cannot be proven in court -- and the facts they are based on cannot be denied.

"In my view for the sake of the country, for the sake of the law, for the sake of the respect of the country's sons and citizens, the prime minister must stand up, resign and go. The public must hold new elections," Peres said.

At a news conference earlier, prosecutors announced they had decided not to charge Netanyahu in connection with the short-lived appointment in January of attorney general Roni Bar-On, a Likud political crony.

But State Prosecutor Edna Arbel said at the news conference that many of the allegations raised by the news media about the affair had proven to be true. She said investigators found that Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, a key member of Netanyahu's coalition, had been interested in appointing Bar-On and had made it clear Shas might withhold its support for Israel's troop redeployment from Hebron unless the lawyer got the job.
